approach.method_basis: The Parent searches a tree of partial SMILES strings. It initializes each objective's tree from the supplied scored molecules, chooses token branches using their average accepted return and an upper confidence exploration bonus, and expands branches supported by a corpus-trained language model. That model remains frozen and completes selected prefixes into whole molecules. Accepted scores update the generating paths. To fill a proposal batch, the Parent selects a block of rollout paths before generating their completions, using the same completed-observation counts for every selection in that block.
approach.novelty: Add pending-path counts to UCT so each selected rollout reserves its path before the next path is chosen. The exploration bonus then accounts for both completed and outstanding work, while average rewards continue to use accepted observations. Reservations disappear when a rollout is discarded or its feedback arrives. This tests whether acknowledging work already assigned reduces repeated sampling from one prefix during a batch. This lineage currently contains only the Parent; no sibling has tested pending-aware selection.

hypothesis: Reserve each selected rollout along its prefix path and include completed plus pending counts in UCT's exploration term, while retaining accepted-only empirical reward means; release each reservation when the rollout is discarded or its observation resolves.

finding_summary.headline: Reservations spread evaluated rollouts across prefixes; the screening score falls
finding_summary.insights: Delayed-feedback concentration is controllable with the existing frozen generator and accepted-only reward estimates. The controlled replay establishes that outstanding work changes actual choices, and the emitted-molecule analysis establishes that the added branch coverage survives invalid, duplicate and surplus filtering. However, almost complete dispersion across ten starting prefixes did not produce a better overall best molecule within the screening budget. This leaves the useful balance between branch reuse and wider allocation open; the score losses do not establish that reservations are generally harmful. The molecular assessment found broadly diverse ring chemistry comparable to the Parent, with useful amine and heteroaromatic motifs already reachable but inconsistent control of their arrangement and whole-molecule growth. That narrows the unresolved problem to obtaining and refining useful chemical combinations: a larger count of distinct SMILES prefixes alone does not establish better chemical coverage. These structural observations suggest an explanation to investigate, not a demonstrated cause of the score decrease. One seed supports activation and a mixed score outcome, without establishing reproducibility or which degree of allocation spread would improve final Top-1.
finding_summary.results: On the single paired screening seed, pending work changed 4,361 of 5,834 branch decisions with a choice between eligible children (74.75%). Of these changes, 3,961 came from altered UCT rankings among completed children; another 400 involved priority for children without completed observations. All 2,900 reservations resolved exactly once, without negative counts, leaks or changes to completed reward statistics. Mean concentration of evaluated rollout-start prefixes fell from 0.809379 to 0.117517 across 145 batches, and distinct prefixes per ten-molecule batch rose from 1.73 to 9.54. Single-prefix batches fell from 76 of 145 to zero, with lower concentration on all five objectives and every paired batch. Both runs delivered all 1,450 valid, unique optimizer proposals within the same oracle budget and retained identical frozen prior weights. The macro final Top-1 score nevertheless fell from 0.479189 to 0.473468, a decrease of 0.005720. Final scores rose for zaleplon_mpo (0.394920 to 0.409811), drd2_docking (0.977922 to 0.999998), and median_2 (0.179942 to 0.180094), while deco_hop fell from 0.606003 to 0.580076 and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.237157 to 0.197364. The proposed allocation mechanism is confirmed; its expected positive score effect was not observed.

molecular.headline: Diverse aromatic and saturated ring chemistry; missing stereochemical specification and consistent control of useful motif arrangements.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied seed-0 trajectories and their Parent counterparts were read; no task lacks a trajectory. Each current trajectory contains 300 unique molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. Evaluation numbers below refer to these current trajectories unless explicitly marked Parent. The proposals are predominantly ring-containing medicinal-chemistry-like structures: linked phenyl and aza-aromatic rings, fused heterocycles, piperidines, piperazines, amides, sulfonamides, ethers, phenols and occasional highly elaborate polycycles. The digest ring-closure occurrence rates are 0.9897 to 1.0 and aromatic-token occurrence rates are 0.9517 to 0.9862; these are fractions of proposal strings containing the relevant tokens, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths are 37.6 to 39.8 characters, with task maxima from 70 to 87 characters; these are size proxies, not molecular weights. Structural breadth is real and comparable to the Parent, including both aromatic and saturated ring families. Basic cyclic amines are clearly present and must not be called globally missing. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0, even though some structures contain potentially stereogenic saturated frameworks. The major deficits are unassigned stereochemistry, inconsistent arrangement of already available polar and aromatic motifs, and excursions into oversized or chemically awkward assemblies. Common scaffolds look makeable in principle, but the peroxyester, unusual imine/imidic-acid representations, densely substituted fused systems and very large appendages justify a questionable overall synthesis reading. This is a structural assessment of the supplied seed, not a synthetic-route validation or an activation judgement.

per_task.generated_character: Ring-rich aromatic and heteroaromatic molecules dominate: ring_closure_rate 0.9966, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9586 and mean SMILES length 39.3. Evaluation 64 is a fused sulfur/nitrogen heterocycle with an oxo group, hydroxymethyl substituent and aminomethyl-linked biphenyl; evaluation 89 is an aminomethyl biphenyl bearing a fluorobenzamide; evaluation 264 is an N-acylated, partly saturated fused nitrogen ring system. The initial indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 already combines a compact aromatic framework with amide and methoxy groups. These are recognisable small-molecule scaffold combinations, although fused-core preparation and substitution selectivity would need examination. The low end includes a long-chain phosphorus-acid/thioether assembly, a large polyaryl polyamine and a tiny nitrotriazole. Rings and functional-group variety are abundant; stereochemical assignments are absent.
liabilities: Evaluation 15 couples extensive hydrocarbon growth to multiple phosphorus-acid oxygens, while evaluation 183 combines large aromatic bulk with several amine-containing appendages; both illustrate poor control of whole-molecule size and polarity.

The dibrominated, multiply substituted cyclopentene at evaluation 38 and the elaborate fused systems raise substitution-selectivity and stereochemical preparation questions even though their graphs were accepted.
missing_features: Most weak examples lack the balanced, intermediate-sized aromatic-plus-polar arrangement visible in the stronger examples: some are too small and sparsely decorated, while others carry long chains or excessive appended ring systems.

A controlled set of close variants preserving a promising ring arrangement while adjusting heteroatom position, linker length or polar substituents is not demonstrated by the cited high and final examples. Their diversity does not identify one additional mandatory functional group.

Explicit stereochemical specification is missing from the substituted saturated frameworks, including evaluation 38. The supplied scores do not establish whether specifying it would improve this objective.

method_name: ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior
method_thesis: Anchor the root in [ChemTS](https://arxiv.org/html/1710.00616v1): train a compact autoregressive SMILES model solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze it. For each independent objective, maintain a fresh prefix tree whose nodes hold visit counts and observed returns. Initialize its statistics from the supplied observations. Select prefixes through upper-confidence tree search, expand them using the frozen model's next-token distribution, and generate complete molecules by stochastic continuation. Backpropagate accepted oracle scores through the corresponding paths after feedback. Generate further continuations until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. This is an expanding generative tree, with no corpus ranking or fixed molecular candidate set. The hypothesis is that sharing each scarce reward across its visited prefixes directs subsequent continuations toward promising molecular families quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. The root adapts tree statistics; it does not update neural parameters with rewards. The paper supports this search mechanism, but its larger, time-limited experiments do not establish performance under this benchmark's scarce feedback. Learning a useful rollout prior within permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

retained_mechanisms: Corpus-only autoregressive SMILES RNN training and frozen task-time rollout weights
Fresh task-local prefix tree initialized from accepted initial observations
UCT with accepted-only empirical reward means, exploration constant 0.5 and inherited tie-breaking rules
Prior-supported prefix expansion, zero-completed-visit stopping and stochastic batched RNN continuation
Canonical identity filtering with bounded retries for valid unique submissions
Accepted-only completed-visit, online-visit and score-sum backups along generating paths
Immediate per-path reservations with pending-aware unvisited priority and exploration counts, explicit unobserved zero initialization, and release on discard or resolved feedback

activation_observables.measurement: The Parent has zero selection-relevant pending counts. Reconstruct every reservation from its selected path: each acquisition increments all path counts by one before the next path selection; each discard or resolved observation decrements that same path exactly once. Require positive pending counts during generation, nonnegative counts everywhere, root pending equal to unresolved provisional plus emitted reservations, and zero remaining counts after fully resolved feedback. Reservation operations must leave completed visits, online visits and score sums unchanged; accepted observations must still back up exactly once.
activation_observables.name: pending_path_reservation_lifecycle

activation_observables.measurement: Recompute pending-aware UCT and its unvisited set from each selection receipt. Count choices made with positive pending counts and at least two eligible children, and the fraction that differ from the completed-only counterfactual using the same eligible set, completed statistics and cloned pre-choice RNG state. Report deterministic ranking changes separately from changed prior-weighted unvisited choices. Require a positive count of changed choices under these controlled local comparisons; they measure the reservation contribution within the Child's trajectory, not a counterfactual oracle result.
activation_observables.name: pending_counts_change_uct_selection

activation_observables.measurement: For each emitted batch, group molecules by their generating rollout-start prefix and compute sum((prefix_count/emitted_count)^2), matching the Parent's definition. Report per-task and pooled means, distinct prefixes per batch and the fraction of single-prefix batches. Compare each available paired seed with the Parent; its supplied screening baseline is 0.809379310345 mean concentration and 76/145 single-prefix batches. Separate selected raw-rollout concentration from emitted concentration so invalid, duplicate and unused surplus draws cannot masquerade as evaluated branch coverage.
activation_observables.name: within_batch_rollout_prefix_concentration

finding_summary.headline: Reservations spread evaluated rollouts across prefixes; the screening score falls
finding_summary.insights: Delayed-feedback concentration is controllable with the existing frozen generator and accepted-only reward estimates. The controlled replay establishes that outstanding work changes actual choices, and the emitted-molecule analysis establishes that the added branch coverage survives invalid, duplicate and surplus filtering. However, almost complete dispersion across ten starting prefixes did not produce a better overall best molecule within the screening budget. This leaves the useful balance between branch reuse and wider allocation open; the score losses do not establish that reservations are generally harmful. The molecular assessment found broadly diverse ring chemistry comparable to the Parent, with useful amine and heteroaromatic motifs already reachable but inconsistent control of their arrangement and whole-molecule growth. That narrows the unresolved problem to obtaining and refining useful chemical combinations: a larger count of distinct SMILES prefixes alone does not establish better chemical coverage. These structural observations suggest an explanation to investigate, not a demonstrated cause of the score decrease. One seed supports activation and a mixed score outcome, without establishing reproducibility or which degree of allocation spread would improve final Top-1.
finding_summary.results: On the single paired screening seed, pending work changed 4,361 of 5,834 branch decisions with a choice between eligible children (74.75%). Of these changes, 3,961 came from altered UCT rankings among completed children; another 400 involved priority for children without completed observations. All 2,900 reservations resolved exactly once, without negative counts, leaks or changes to completed reward statistics. Mean concentration of evaluated rollout-start prefixes fell from 0.809379 to 0.117517 across 145 batches, and distinct prefixes per ten-molecule batch rose from 1.73 to 9.54. Single-prefix batches fell from 76 of 145 to zero, with lower concentration on all five objectives and every paired batch. Both runs delivered all 1,450 valid, unique optimizer proposals within the same oracle budget and retained identical frozen prior weights. The macro final Top-1 score nevertheless fell from 0.479189 to 0.473468, a decrease of 0.005720. finding_summary.headline: Reservations spread evaluated rollouts across prefixes; the screening score falls
finding_summary.insights: Delayed-feedback concentration is controllable with the existing frozen generator and accepted-only reward estimates. The controlled replay establishes that outstanding work changes actual choices, and the emitted-molecule analysis establishes that the added branch coverage survives invalid, duplicate and surplus filtering. However, almost complete dispersion across ten starting prefixes did not produce a better overall best molecule within the screening budget. This leaves the useful balance between branch reuse and wider allocation open; the score losses do not establish that reservations are generally harmful. The molecular assessment found broadly diverse ring chemistry comparable to the Parent, with useful amine and heteroaromatic motifs already reachable but inconsistent control of their arrangement and whole-molecule growth. That narrows the unresolved problem to obtaining and refining useful chemical combinations: a larger count of distinct SMILES prefixes alone does not establish better chemical coverage. These structural observations suggest an explanation to investigate, not a demonstrated cause of the score decrease. One seed supports activation and a mixed score outcome, without establishing reproducibility or which degree of allocation spread would improve final Top-1.
finding_summary.results: On the single paired screening seed, pending work changed 4,361 of 5,834 branch decisions with a choice between eligible children (74.75%). Of these changes, 3,961 came from altered UCT rankings among completed children; another 400 involved priority for children without completed observations. All 2,900 reservations resolved exactly once, without negative counts, leaks or changes to completed reward statistics. Mean concentration of evaluated rollout-start prefixes fell from 0.809379 to 0.117517 across 145 batches, and distinct prefixes per ten-molecule batch rose from 1.73 to 9.54. Single-prefix batches fell from 76 of 145 to zero, with lower concentration on all five objectives and every paired batch. Both runs delivered all 1,450 valid, unique optimizer proposals within the same oracle budget and retained identical frozen prior weights. The macro final Top-1 score nevertheless fell from 0.479189 to 0.473468, a decrease of 0.005720. Final scores rose for zaleplon_mpo (0.394920 to 0.409811), drd2_docking (0.977922 to 0.999998), and median_2 (0.179942 to 0.180094), while deco_hop fell from 0.606003 to 0.580076 and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.237157 to 0.197364. The proposed allocation mechanism is confirmed; its expected positive score effect was not observed.

molecular_assessment.headline: Diverse aromatic and saturated ring chemistry; missing stereochemical specification and consistent control of useful motif arrangements.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All five supplied seed-0 trajectories and their Parent counterparts were read; no task lacks a trajectory. Each current trajectory contains 300 unique molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. Evaluation numbers below refer to these current trajectories unless explicitly marked Parent. The proposals are predominantly ring-containing medicinal-chemistry-like structures: linked phenyl and aza-aromatic rings, fused heterocycles, piperidines, piperazines, amides, sulfonamides, ethers, phenols and occasional highly elaborate polycycles. The digest ring-closure occurrence rates are 0.9897 to 1.0 and aromatic-token occurrence rates are 0.9517 to 0.9862; these are fractions of proposal strings containing the relevant tokens, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths are 37.6 to 39.8 characters, with task maxima from 70 to 87 characters; these are size proxies, not molecular weights. Structural breadth is real and comparable to the Parent, including both aromatic and saturated ring families. Basic cyclic amines are clearly present and must not be called globally missing. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0, even though some structures contain potentially stereogenic saturated frameworks. The major deficits are unassigned stereochemistry, inconsistent arrangement of already available polar and aromatic motifs, and excursions into oversized or chemically awkward assemblies. Common scaffolds look makeable in principle, but the peroxyester, unusual imine/imidic-acid representations, densely substituted fused systems and very large appendages justify a questionable overall synthesis reading. This is a structural assessment of the supplied seed, not a synthetic-route validation or an activation judgement.
